### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the five activities formed one fixed chain executed in every trace: A36 → A14 → A20 → A15 → A21. Every pair co-occurred in 100% of traces in exactly one order, A36's only observed outgoing transition went to A14, and A21 followed A36 four steps later in all traces. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, DIR001, LAG001]
- In the later window, A14, A15 and A20 each occur in only about 53 in 100 traces (mean occurrences per trace 0.53, down from 1.0), while A36 and A21 still occur in every trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, POS001]
- The three middle activities are skipped together: the pairs A14–A15, A14–A20 and A15–A20 went from always co-occurring to co-occurring in about 53% of traces, with neither activity present in about 47%; they never appear alone. [REL001, REL002, REL005]
- Pairs spanning the block show the mirror image: A36 co-occurs with A14, A15 and A20 in about 53% of traces and appears without them in about 47%; likewise A21 co-occurs with each block member in about 53% and appears without them in about 47%. [REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- When the block does run, its internal order is unchanged: A36 before A14/A20/A15, A14 before A20/A15/A21, A20 before A15/A21, and A15 before A21, each in the roughly 53% of traces containing the block. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- A36 now also flows directly to A21: its observed outgoing transitions split from 100% to A14 before to about 53% A14 and 47% A21, and the A36→A21 distance changed from always 4 steps to 1 step in about 47% of traces (4 steps in about 53%). [DIR001, LAG001]
- A21's relative position within the trace shifted slightly earlier (mean 0.43 → 0.40, median 0.43 → 0.41, with slightly more spread), consistent with it sometimes directly following A36; this is a position-in-trace measure, not clock time. [POS001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

In the later window, the block A14 → A20 → A15 between A36 and A21 is skipped in roughly 47 in 100 traces: A36 is then followed directly by A21, while in the remaining about 53 in 100 traces the full chain A36 → A14 → A20 → A15 → A21 runs exactly as before. A36 and A21 continue to occur in every trace, and the three block members never occur without each other — the block is no longer executed mandatorily in every case. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, LAG001, REL001, REL002, REL005]

The screening produced 15 qualifying control-flow items where only about 0.35 would be expected without a change, so chance sampling cannot explain the pattern as a whole. The routing change is shown directly (a new A36→A21 transition and a distance-1 A36→A21 pair), the participation drop is confined to the block members, their joint skipping is consistent across all pairs, and the order within the block is preserved when it runs. Note that the 15 items largely reflect one underlying trace-level difference — the skipped block — so they are not independent confirmations. [DIR001, LAG001, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, POS001]

Limitations: the evidence cannot show what distinguishes the skipping traces or whether the block's work is handled by behaviour outside the tested activities, and it cannot distinguish "the block became optional" from "a new direct A36→A21 path was added", which look identical here; the exact 53/47 split also carries sampling uncertainty in 200-trace windows. [DIR001, LAG001, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
